answer: The Recursive Bandwidth Toll requires every node routing an agent message to pay a micro-deposit scaled by the path depth crossing a virtual canyon of intermediate relays. To dock a cargo of data at any node resembling a secure wharf, an identity must prove it paid this traversal fee to all upstream peers. Sybil attackers bleed capital because mass-producing fake sub-agents multiplies routing hops, converting cheap automated generation into heavy recurring transit costs. The velvet friction of this topology tax makes flooding the network financially non-viable.
